nodes.label: renderViewerHtml
nodes.rationale: The only supported way to generate a page around the viewer; the raw html string export is deprecated because its formatting changes between releases and pattern-matching it is unsupported. inlineCss/inlineJs yield a single self-contained file with the splat as a data: URI named via contentFilename, since the splat format is chosen by the name's extension and a data: URI has no filename.

nodes.label: createViewer
nodes.source_location: Creating a viewer in your own page
nodes.rationale: The /viewer subpath entry with playcanvas as a peer dependency so the host's engine copy is the one used. Resolves once the graphics device exists and loading has started, not once the scene is visible; the viewer builds its own subtree so the container needs a size or nothing renders.

nodes.label: Viewer Handle
nodes.rationale: Host and built-in playback controls use the same API: observable state with writable keys that apply at once plus <key>:changed events. Nothing is published to window unless exposeGlobals is set; keyboard/gamepad listeners cannot be routed by hit-testing, so hosts gate them with state.inputEnabled.

nodes.label: captureFrame
nodes.rationale: Renders offscreen, supersampled, waits for the first frame, and resolves { width, height, data } with base64 data.

nodes.label: seek
nodes.rationale: Synchronous and preserves pause state, so pause first to stop at the requested time; wraps repeat tracks and clamps once and ping-pong tracks to their duration. The standalone window.scrubTo hook retains pause-and-wait-for-frame behavior instead.

nodes.label: selectAnnotation
nodes.rationale: The same command the built-in hotspots and previous/next buttons use; null clears selection without starting another camera movement; runtime annotation editing is unsupported and the data is read-only in settings order.

nodes.label: setMoveInput
nodes.rationale: An explicit command that works independently of gamingControls, inputMode and inputEnabled; values clamp to [-1,1] and stay active until replaced, and the viewer clears held input on camera/XR mode changes, window blur, visibility changes and destruction. The built-in touch joystick uses the same command.

nodes.label: Camera Commands (frameScene / resetCamera / toggleWalk)
nodes.rationale: Throw before state.loaded or after destruction, matching seek; frameScene now reports invalid calls instead of silently doing nothing. toggleWalk reproduces the built-in walk button, returning to the previous mode including one the host entered by writing state directly.

nodes.label: Fullscreen & XR Commands (requestFullscreen / startXR / endXR)
nodes.rationale: startXR never reloads the page - the built-in UI owns the WebGL reload prompt; the legacy iframe fullscreen parent-message bridge resolves when sent because it has no acknowledgement; standalone headsets render with fixed foveation, 72 Hz target and a 1 million splat budget (0.8x resolution in performance mode).

nodes.label: destroy
nodes.rationale: Browsers cap live WebGL contexts at around 16, so a component that mounts and unmounts without tearing down will stop rendering; destroy is idempotent, releases the engine application, graphics context, every listener, the subtree, and rejects outstanding API waits.

nodes.label: ExperienceSettings Schema
nodes.rationale: settings.json v2 schema defined in TypeScript and exported from the /settings subpath; legacy v1 settings produced by older SuperSplat releases are automatically migrated forward on load.

nodes.label: defaultSettings
nodes.rationale: Returns a complete settings object every tool agrees on; pass 'object' to frame a subject from outside rather than a captured space from within.

nodes.label: validateSettings
nodes.rationale: Throws on invalid input naming the offending field; the { limits: true } authoring-bounds check is stricter than what the viewer will render (existing files may fail) and producers writing new settings should enable it.

nodes.label: importSettings
nodes.rationale: Migrates older settings versions forward without mutating its argument.

nodes.label: POST_EFFECT_RANGES
nodes.rationale: Bounds (with CAMERA_FOV_RANGE, ANIM_TRACK_LIMITS, ANNOTATION_LIMITS) are exported as frozen data so an editor UI can drive sliders from the same numbers the validator uses.

nodes.label: Saved Preferences
nodes.rationale: performanceMode, gamingControls and showAnnotations load from and write to existing origin-wide localStorage keys with or without the built-in UI; creation does not write defaults; the legacy retinaDisplay migration is preserved; storage denial or quota errors leave the viewer usable; already-mounted viewers keep their own state rather than syncing through storage; destruction removes persistence subscriptions.
